prompt: It slowly falls into ruin unless I visit and care for it.

card.name: The Tended Hold

site.text: An ordinary settlement on level ground within the claim, left open for the player's own choice of place.

style.text: Weathered, half-overgrown stone and timber that looks cared for in places and slowly crumbling in others; moss, cracked bricks, vines.

purpose.text: A home base the player keeps alive by visiting and caring for it; it decays when neglected.

story.text: It slowly falls into ruin unless I visit and care for it.

card.interpretation: You gave only a story: the place decays unless you visit and care for it. I read that as a home base in a ruined style, so it looks tended in places and crumbling in others. Site is ordinary flat ground, medium size, with no specific place named.

contradictions.issue: Decay over time depends on game mechanics, not on a built structure.
contradictions.resolution: The card shows a ruined, partly repaired look; the actual decay over time is left to later modules.

assumptions: Home base purpose, since you return to care for it.
Ruined style chosen for the sense of decay.
Flat village layout on level ground.
Location is searched near the claim.

program.notes: The heart of the place, where the player returns; best-kept building, with a hearth and a bed.
Small homes in varying states of repair, some with fallen roofs and mossy walls.
Where repairs are made; tool racks and anvil, partly collapsed chimney.
Stores repair materials: stone, timber, glass; sagging roof.
Overgrown plots a visitor could tend.
Half-ruined, roof open to the sky, a quiet place of remembrance.
Leaning entrance, the first sight of how neglected the place is.
